content: Spec writing: 2-lead structure with research lead + spec-writer lead. Research lead sends findings via mail, writer lead spawns builder for draft then reviser to integrate research. Avoids file conflicts, enables iteration.

M0 scaffolding: single lead with single builder is sufficient. M1 implementation: split into 2 parallel leads by file area (scanner vs graph/cache/CLI). Non-overlapping file scopes prevent merge conflicts. Graph lead merged first, parsing lead took longer due to tree-sitter complexity + 2 stalled builders before successful 3rd attempt.

M2 decomposition: 2 leads (WASM/layout vs web/server). WASM lead finished first (simpler Rust-only). Web lead split into rust-server-builder + web-ui-builder (3 attempts needed for JS/TS builder — complex npm/bundling tasks stall builders frequently). Merge order matters when builders share files: merge server first, then UI (UI has definitive main.ts).

name: merge-conflict-entry-function
description: Auto-resolve merge conflicts can silently keep wrong version when two builders modify the same file. Always verify run()/main entry points after merging overlapping branches — helpers may survive while the entry function gets replaced with a stub.

name: cycles-parallel-decomposition
description: Cycles feature: 2-builder parallel decomposition (Rust backend + web frontend) under single lead. Non-overlapping file areas prevented merge conflicts. Both branches merged cleanly to main.

name: p2-features-3-lead-decomposition
description: P2 features batch (4 features, 3 leads): orphan-lead (core+CLI, fast), features-backend-lead (annotations+snapshot Rust, medium), web-features-lead (all 4 UI features, large). Non-overlapping file areas: lead1=graph/orphans+scan.rs, lead2=annotations.rs+annotate.rs+snapshot.rs+routes.rs+main.rs, lead3=all web/ files. Clean merges, no conflicts.
